summary:
Alpha Agro - Earth System Intelligence for Agriculture

Alpha Agro is an Earth observation and agricultural intelligence platform that transforms NASA environmental data into accessible scientific insights for Argentina's Pampas region.

Using GLDAS soil-moisture data and other Earth system variables, the platform analyzes historical trends, environmental relationships, spatial patterns, and uncertainty.

It also explores machine learning and probabilistic forecasting using XGBoost, Hidden Markov Models, and statistical baselines.

Our goal is to help farmers, researchers, and decision-makers better understand soil-water conditions and potential agricultural risks.

Historical predictive results are evaluated using time-aware validation. Operational forecasting remains an ongoing research objective.
details:
Alpha Agro — From Earth Data to Agricultural Insight

Alpha Agro is an Earth observation and agricultural intelligence platform that transforms NASA environmental data into accessible scientific insights and experimental predictive information for agricultural decision-making.

Our project focuses on Argentina's Pampas region, one of the country's most important agricultural areas, where variations in soil moisture, precipitation, and temperature can significantly affect farming conditions.

What does Alpha Agro do?

Alpha Agro combines historical Earth system analysis, machine learning, and interactive visualization in a single web application.

Using NASA's GLDAS Noah land surface model, we analyzed 20 years of monthly environmental data (2006–2025) across approximately 896 geographical grid cells at 0.25° spatial resolution.

The platform allows users to explore:

  • Historical trends: How soil-water storage has changed over time, including statistical significance and uncertainty.
  • Environmental relationships: How precipitation, temperature, evapotranspiration, and runoff relate to soil-water conditions.
  • Spatial patterns: How environmental conditions differ across geographical locations.
  • Predictive research: Retrospective predictions of soil-water storage, anomalies, and low-moisture events at one-, two-, and three-month horizons.
  • Model comparisons: Transparent evaluations of machine learning methods against simple statistical benchmarks.

Rather than displaying predictions without context, Alpha Agro emphasizes how reliable those predictions are and whether more complex algorithms actually improve performance.

How does it work?

Our scientific pipeline processes NASA environmental datasets using Python, transforming raw observations and modeled variables into reproducible regional and spatial datasets.

We use statistical methods to investigate trends, relationships, autocorrelation, and uncertainty.

For predictive modeling, we implemented and evaluated several approaches:

  • Seasonal climatology and persistence baselines.
  • Ridge regression.
  • XGBoost machine learning.
  • Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) for identifying latent environmental regimes and providing forward-filtered features.

Models are evaluated using time-aware walk-forward validation and a reserved historical holdout period. This helps reduce lookahead bias and provides a more realistic assessment of predictive performance.

An important finding is that more complex models do not automatically outperform simpler approaches. Seasonal climatology remained the selected model across our 18 evaluated combinations of geographical scope, prediction horizon, and target variable.

We consider this transparency a central feature of Alpha Agro: the platform communicates both what the data reveals and what the evidence cannot yet establish.

What benefits does it provide?

Alpha Agro makes complex Earth observation data easier to interpret for farmers, agricultural researchers, students, and decision-makers.

Potential benefits include:

  • Improving access to historical soil-moisture information.
  • Identifying geographical patterns of unusually dry or wet conditions.
  • Understanding relationships between environmental variables.
  • Exploring early indicators of agricultural water stress.
  • Supporting research into more informed planting and water-management decisions.
  • Making predictive uncertainty and model limitations visible.

Our long-term objective is to support agricultural planning for crops such as soybean, maize, and wheat.

What makes Alpha Agro innovative?

Alpha Agro combines Earth system science, quantitative modeling, and agricultural decision intelligence.

Instead of simply presenting satellite imagery or environmental charts, we developed a reproducible research pipeline that connects NASA data with statistical inference, spatial analysis, machine learning, and uncertainty evaluation.

Our approach is also deliberately evidence-driven. We test sophisticated models against simple baselines, preserve the distinction between correlation and causation, and explicitly identify when predictive improvements are not statistically established.

The application is designed to evolve toward prospective forecasting, using verified NASA data availability and timestamped model predictions. Operational forecasting is not yet claimed: the current predictive results are historical evaluations and retrospective forecasts.

Technologies and tools

Programming and data science

  • Python
  • Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, and statistical modeling tools
  • XGBoost and scikit-learn
  • Hidden Markov Models
  • Parquet and JSON data formats

Web development

  • React
  • TypeScript
  • Vite
  • Interactive scientific dashboards and visualizations

Data sources

  • NASA GLDAS Noah v2.1
  • NASA Earth observation products investigated for future data integration, including IMERG, POWER, and SMAP

Development infrastructure

  • Git and GitHub
  • Visual Studio Code
  • Windows-based development computers
  • Automated testing and reproducible research workflows

What factors did we consider?

We focused on five principles:

Scientific reliability: Statistical uncertainty, proper validation, and honest interpretation of results.

Temporal integrity: Preventing models from using information that would not have been available at prediction time.

Accessibility: Translating complex environmental information into understandable visualizations.

Agricultural relevance: Focusing on soil-water conditions that may influence agricultural planning in the Argentine Pampas.

Reproducibility: Maintaining versioned datasets, documented methodologies, automated tests, and traceable model evaluations.

Intended impact

Our vision is to make Earth system intelligence more accessible and useful for agriculture.

By connecting NASA environmental data with transparent statistical analysis and predictive research, Alpha Agro aims to help users understand changing soil-water conditions, investigate environmental risks, and eventually support more informed agricultural decisions.

We believe that the future of agricultural intelligence should not depend on increasingly complex models alone, but on combining reliable data, rigorous science, understandable uncertainty, and accessible technology.

Alpha Agro: From Earth Data to Agricultural Insight.
